newsitem.title: UK: UK rate rise won't hit housing recovery - RICs.
newsitem.headline: UK rate rise won't hit housing recovery - RICs.

text.p: A quarter-point rise in British interest rates will not harm the housing market recovery but any further increases will impoverish homeowners and widen the north/south regional divide, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said on Tuesday.

The abolition of tax relief on mortgage interest payments (MIRAS), a move Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown is tipped to introduce in his first budget, would also widen the divide, it said.
"Further (rate) rises, if coupled with the abolition of MIRAS, would leave thousands of homeowners worse off and widen the north/south divide," it said.
Brown sanctioned a quarter-point rate rise, taking base rates to 6.25 percent, earlier on Tuesday.
The RICs said house prices have risen throughout the country over the past 18 months with the market in London and the South East booming.
"MIRAS is more significant to homeowners in the north as it only covers the first 30,000 stg of a mortgage," the RICs said. Houses are still cheaper in the north than south of the country.
"We look forward to the new government clarifying its position on MIRAS," said RICs economist Matthew Ryall. "If, as predicted, it is phased out, we could see a widening of the north/south divide."
